collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: An elder asks to be buried by the sea instead of the graveyard when the time comes: agree, or ask the village first.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has spent (subject.his/her) whole life on the water, and has asked (friend) for a promise: when (subject.he/she) dies, (subject.he/she) wants to be buried on the headland, where the sea can be heard, and not in the graveyard with everyone else. (friend) is not sure the village will allow it. What should (friend) do?

text_only.reason: a death only talked about (or the word's everyday sense); nobody dies -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) promises. (subject) is satisfied, and spends the next season planting flowers on the headland, getting the place ready, and complaining about the soil. (friend) helps, and says nothing to anyone.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) brings it to the gathering. There is a long discussion. In the end the village agrees, and several other old fishers ask for the same. The headland becomes the fishers' resting place. (subject) is very smug about having thought of it first.
